Finbox

Finbox is a fintech company that allows you to embed lending infratstructure in your application.

Finbox's Landing Page

React Static 15

I worked on the landing page and the entire website from scratch. Using react-static, I generated static pages with SPA navigation.

I also organized Design Sprints to target specific audiences

Started from scratch with UI/UX to develop a unique brand identity for the company. Made personalized icons. illustrations, animations, etc.

This was my first opportunity to design and build a decently sized website.

  • The website contained several bespoke components that I had to structure and develop from scratch.
  • The image gallery is one such example, with the tricky part being making it responsive.
  • The developer section caters to developers (duh!).
  • It has the same style as the rest of the website but incorporates a developer terminal to showcase the features.
  • The features section is a standard icon title description grid, sometimes displayed as cards, but here has been stripped down to the bare minimum.
  • The enterprise section highlights information about certifications and large eneterprise customers.
  • I also designed most of the illustrations including this isometric hero illustration which I made in Figma.
  • There were several illustrations made that were not used in the final version.
  • We worked with the wireframes first to ideate over the structure and layout of the website.
  • The colors and typography were chosen to depict a serious modern fintech startup.
  • I created several accompanying pages like the about page.
  • They usually carried the same style but had different layouts.
  • The contact page was designed specifically to avoid the usual bland form.
  • It is still there, but housed in a quite pleasing layout.
  • A product page highlights the features of a specific product.
  • It is usually similar to the homepage but a bit more focused.
  • A mobile article page prototype with an enticing cover image.
  • A blog post page with a bit of content.
  • The typography of the blog posts was chosen to be serif intentionally.
  • A blog post displayed on a large screen.
  • It utilizes the whitespaces evenly and is balanced throughout.
  • The same post transforms to the slender screen of mobiles.
  • Here the small mistake of extra horizontal padding in the title and context can be noticed.
  • For I had not gained expertise in design back then.
